options.content:
**Model drift** here does **not** mean "the model got the wrong answer" -- nobody labels incoming reviews in real time, so there's no way to check that directly. It means: does live traffic *look* like the traffic the model was evaluated on? A shift is a signal worth a human look, not proof the model is broken.

**How it's measured -- PSI (Population Stability Index):** one number per signal, comparing the current distribution of a value (e.g. how confident predictions are) against the training-time baseline. This project reads it with the usual convention:
- **< 0.10** -> `ok` -- looks like training
- **0.10 - 0.25** -> `warning` -- some shift, worth watching
- **>= 0.25** -> `alert` -- meaningfully different from training

New to PSI? [Arize: Population Stability Index (PSI) explained](https://arize.com/blog-course/population-stability-index-psi/) is a good plain-English start. For where PSI can mislead you, see [NannyML: PSI or not PSI?](https://nannymlnewsletter.substack.com/p/psi-or-not-psi-that-is-the-question)

Every check needs **30+ predictions** in its time window to produce a real number -- below that it reports `insufficient_data` (see the Sample size panel) rather than guessing. Use the time range picker (top right) to zoom in on any window -- every panel below respects it.

panels.title: PSI per signal over time
panels.description: One line per signal (prediction confidence, review length). Left-to-right is time; up is "more different from the training baseline." The colored threshold lines mark 0.10 (warning) and 0.25 (alert) -- a line crossing into orange/red territory is the thing to investigate. A flat line near zero is the healthy, expected state.

targets.rawSql: SELECT checked_at AS time, prediction_confidence_psi, review_length_psi FROM drift_checks WHERE $__timeFilter(checked_at) ORDER BY checked_at

panels.title: Status over time
panels.description: One colored block per drift check (roughly every 2 minutes in the cloud deployment). Green = ok, orange = warning, red = alert -- whichever of the two PSI signals scores worse decides the color. A single red block might just be a traffic blip; a run of them is the real signal worth investigating.

targets.rawSql: SELECT checked_at AS time, status AS value FROM drift_checks WHERE $__timeFilter(checked_at) ORDER BY checked_at

panels.title: Sample size per check
panels.description: How many predictions fed each check. Below 30 (the dashed threshold line), a check can't produce a trustworthy PSI at all and reports "insufficient_data" instead -- a dip here explains an "insufficient_data" status in the panel above, it isn't a separate problem.

targets.rawSql: SELECT checked_at AS time, sample_size FROM drift_checks WHERE $__timeFilter(checked_at) ORDER BY checked_at
